questions.q: In the "trust dilemma" story, what real problem is the town actually trying to solve?
options: No reliable record of transactions exists, so disputes come down to word of mouth
Nobody in the town knows how to use a computer
The town wants to invent a brand-new currency for fun
The town has too much money circulating and needs to reduce it
questions.explain: Alice lends Bob $50, Bob later denies it, and with no documentation the dispute can't be settled fairly — that's the actual trust problem blockchain was built to solve.

questions.q: What real risk do centralized ledger-keepers (banks, notaries, governments) carry?
options: They can't keep any records at all
They're vulnerable to fraud or manipulation, and the whole system depends on that one entity staying honest
They're always completely incorruptible and risk-free
They only work for cryptocurrency, not real money
questions.explain: A centralized system concentrates trust in one entity or small group — if that trust breaks down, the entire system can be subverted.

questions.q: According to the definition given in class, what is a blockchain at its simplest?
options: A programming language used only for smart contracts
A type of cryptocurrency wallet app
A single company's private database of customer purchases
A digital, decentralized ledger that securely records transactions across a network of computers
questions.explain: The core definition is decentralization plus a secure, shared record — not any one company's product or a single currency.

questions.q: Why does changing an old, confirmed block become so impractical?
options: Blocks can only be edited by the original person who created them
Old blocks are automatically deleted after a year
Every block is cryptographically linked to the one before it, so altering one breaks that link across every copy of the ledger
There's no real reason — old blocks are just as easy to edit as new ones
questions.explain: Because each block links to the previous one, and every participant holds an identical copy, rewriting history would require changing every subsequent block on every copy simultaneously without detection.

questions.q: Beyond cryptocurrency, which of these is a real application of blockchain mentioned in this lesson?
options: Supply chain tracking, digital identity, and smart contracts
Only online gaming leaderboards
Word processing software
Blockchain has no real uses outside of Bitcoin
questions.explain: Bitcoin popularized blockchain, but the same underlying idea already supports supply chain tracking, digital identity systems, and smart contracts — Lesson 5 explores real-world examples like this in depth.
